chunks: Muhammad ibn Umar al-Baghdadi al-Hafiz narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Abul Qasim Ishaq ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), saying: He narrated to me his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Alawi, saying: He narrated to me Ali ibn Muhammad al-Alawi, known as al-Mushallal, saying: He informed me Sulayman ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon them both), saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

"Five [things] I will not abandon until death: wearing wool, riding a saddled donkey, eating with the servants, mending my shoe with my hand, and greeting the children, so that these become a Sunnah after me."

key_terms.خِصَافِي النَّعْلَ بِيَدِي: mending my shoe with my hand

ai.seo_question: What are the five things the Prophet said he would not abandon until death?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* via a chain of Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s deliberate preservation of asceticism (*zuhd*) and egalitarianism as active Sunnah rather than mere personal preference. By engaging in manual labor like mending his own shoes and sharing meals with servants, he dismantled class distinctions, while his greeting of children underscored the importance of nurturing the next generation with humility.
